newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin recovering ahead of timetable - surgeon.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin recovering ahead of timetable - surgeon.

text.p: Russian heart surgeon Renat Akchurin, who led the heart bypass operation on Boris Yeltsin, said on Thursday the president was recovering ahead of schedule and could resume most duties within two weeks.
Akchurin said Yeltsin could be ready to talk in public as early as Friday or Saturday.
Yeltsin, 65, has been surprising doctors with the pace of his recovery after Tuesday's quintuple heart bypass surgery.
A relaxed-looking Akchurin said Yeltsin was being monitored intensively at Moscow's Cardiology Research Centre where the operation was performed.

"I think that somewhere around 10 to 12 days after the operation he could quite easily fulfil the major part of his duties," Akchurin said in an interview on NTV commercial television's "Hero of the Day" programme.
The surgeon was optimistic the president would be able to make a public appearance soon.
Asked when Yeltsin himself would be able to talk about the operation, Akchurin said: "Tomorrow, the day after tomorrow".
He said the post-operation timetable for the president had been adjusted due to the rapid pace of Yeltsin's recovery.
"The president has changed our schedule slightly -- he got out of bed and started walking earlier," Akchurin said.
"He gets up, walks around his bed, sits in an armchair, meets with close family, relatives."
Akchurin said there had been no surprises during the surgery and that his team had been not been ruffled over operating on such an important figure.
"Everything that surrounds the patient goes out of your head," he said.
